title: Sentryline throughput gauge & rollout dial — per-route/model dashboard prototype
creator: Asha Patel
description: Objective: design a compact per-route and per-model dashboard panel that makes trade-offs between latency visibility, throughput signals, and token cost explicit. This ticket delivers a high-fidelity prototype (Figma) plus a concise chart spec and interaction notes for the rollout dial (canary controls) that product and eng can implement in Q2. Focus areas: 1) single-row compact header for route summary; 2) a radial throughput gauge + sparkline combo; 3) latency quantile view with selectable quantiles and threshold bands; 4) token waterfall mini-chart with cost overlay; 5) rollout control (dial/slider) with immediate impact preview and safe-fallback flows.
design_notes:
Key UI patterns and rationale:
- Throughput: radial gauge (0–100% of route capacity) paired with 24h sparkline underneath to show recent spikes. Radial chosen for glanceability on runbooks where vertical space is constrained.
- Latency: stacked quantile bands (P50/P95/P99) rendered as translucent range ribbons with a toggle to switch to a violin when sample size > 10k. Rationale: ribbons communicate shifts over time while violin provides distribution detail for heavy-tailed patterns.
- Token waterfall: horizontal stacked bar that decomposes request into prompt/response/tokenized segments with an optional cost overlay and hover micro-breakdowns. Cost shown in micro-dollars per 1k tokens with color-coded delta against baseline model variant.
- Rollout dial: an interactive circular dial / slider that sets canary percentage. Changing the dial animates a small preview of expected throughput and latency signal change (based on model profiles) and warns if chosen variant exceeds cost thresholds. Dial includes quick-presets (5%, 25%, 50%, 100%).
- Accessibility: all visual encodings have text alternatives; color palette passes WCAG AA for key statuses; keyboard controls for the dial (arrow keys to fine-tune).
- Performance trade-offs: violin rendering deferred to client-side worker for >5k samples; default visualization uses quantile ribbons with sampling. Engineering asked for bounded compute; propose server-side aggregation endpoints delivering quantiles and histograms to reduce client load.
- Edge cases: when route has heterogeneous model variants, the header shows a compact chip list with current active variant and a dropdown to open rollout controls. If KV-cache drop is detected, a banner appears with recommended rollback.

2026-02-18 Liam Chen: Eng sync — engineering prefers server-side quantile precomputation. Marking dependency on ENG-2345 for telemetry aggregation API.
2026-02-23 Priya Nair (Design Review): Suggested replacing histogram default with ribbon quantiles for compactness. Requested clearer microcopy for rollout dial safety checks.
2026-02-27 Maya Liu (PM): Asked for explicit cost preview when moving dial past 25% - flagged as high-value request for sales demos. Added label 'token-economics'.
2026-03-02 Oscar Martinez (Accessibility): Reviewed contrast and keyboard behavior; requested focus ring and aria-live updates for rollout preview numbers.

2026-03-05 Liam Chen (Eng): Implementation note — radial gauge will use SVG with incremental updates; violin deferred behind feature flag due to render cost. ENG-6789 created to implement client-side sampling worker.
2026-03-09 Asha Patel: Prototype updated with canary presets, rollback confirmation modal copy, and micro-animations for gauge. Ready for stakeholder usability test next week.
2026-03-10 Priya Nair: In-review feedback: tighten spacing on token waterfall labels, add explicit units for cost overlays, and show placeholder when telemetry sparse (<100 samples).
acceptance_criteria: Figma high-fidelity prototype including compact panel and expanded view linked in ticket
Chart spec doc describing data contract (quantiles, histograms, throughput buckets) and rendering fallbacks
Rollout dial interaction spec with keyboard and screen-reader behavior
PM sign-off on cost preview behavior and microcopy
Engineering acknowledges telemetry contract (ENG-2345) and client-side rendering constraints (ENG-6789)
decision: Adopt ribbon quantiles as default, violin as opt-in for heavy samples; implement radial throughput gauge for compact views; rollout dial will be primary control with preset buttons and cost-preview tooltip. Server-side quantiles required — ENG will expose aggregated endpoints. Deliver for console-2026.04.
